turns.content: I need to determine which of four compounds can exhibit optical isomerism: dimethyl 6,6'-dinitro-[1,1'-biphenyl]-2,2'-dicarboxylate, methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate, benzophenone, and dimethyl fumarate. What structural criteria should I use, including both tetrahedral stereogenic centers and stable axial chirality?
Apply those criteria to dimethyl 6,6'-dinitro-[1,1'-biphenyl]-2,2'-dicarboxylate. Can it exhibit optical isomerism, and which structural feature is decisive?
Now apply the same criteria to methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate. Is it optically active, and what local structural feature controls the answer?
Assess benzophenone and dimethyl fumarate in the same way. Is each molecule chiral or achiral, and why?
Based on those assessments, which compounds can exhibit optical isomerism, and what is the stereogenic element in each?
Why is dimethyl fumarate achiral despite its E geometry, and why does alkene geometry alone not imply optical activity?
Do molecular symmetry and planarity change any of the four classifications? Resolve any remaining borderline case.
How should the biphenyl assignment be qualified when its rotational barrier, temperature, solvent, and observation timescale are not reported?
With that qualification, check all four compounds once more against tetrahedral stereogenic centers, symmetry, planarity, and configurational stability of a biaryl axis.
State the optically active set and include the appropriate qualification about atropisomer stability.
